caption: The drawing depicts a single wooden bench with armrests and a backrest, positioned centrally against a plain, off-white background. The bench is constructed from wood with a natural, light brown tone showing wood grain and some signs of wear. The backrest features four vertical slats with ornamental shapes, each connected at the top and bottom by horizontal wooden beams. The top rail of the backrest is scalloped with a repeating pattern of arched shapes. Both armrests are flat and extend forward, with the left armrest showing more irregular shaping, possibly due to wear or the natural form of the wood. The seat is a flat plank supported by a front beam, and the bench stands on four straight legs. Below the seat, the front of the bench has three additional vertical slats with the same ornamental shapes as those in the backrest, connected between two horizontal beams. In the lower right corner of the drawing, there is a small inscription or signature in red ink.
title: Bench
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
